title: Capacity Conflict in Mesh Topology
description: This scenario explores capacity conflict dynamics within a mesh communication topology. The disturbance creates coordination challenges that test the agents' ability to adapt, communicate effectively, and maintain freight flow under adverse conditions.
edge_cases_to_watch: Multiple agents may attempt to route freight simultaneously
Lower-priority freight must wait or find alternate routes
Coordination required to avoid wasted capacity
Message propagation delay in mesh vs. physical bottleneck synchronization
Deadlock where agents await capacity confirmation that is being consumed by others
Oscillation where agents repeatedly switch between the 'west-east' and 'west-south-east' routes
coordination_challenges: Resource Contention: Resolving which agent claims the limited 2-unit capacity on 'west-east' during the disturbance
Information Asymmetry: Agents seeing local capacity but lacking global view of competing job priorities
Path Redundancy Management: Evaluating if the overhead of the 'west-south-east' detour exceeds the turn-limit penalty of the 'west-east' wait time
Priority Preemption: High-priority agents must signal intent to low-priority agents to force route yielding
suggested_agent_strategies: Auction-based Reservation: Agents bid for capacity slots on contested routes based on job priority and remaining turns
Proactive Rerouting: Low-priority agents preemptively divert to sub-optimal paths (e.g., via north) when high-contention is detected
Consensus-based Scheduling: Agents use the mesh topology to reach a distributed agreement on the 'west-east' schedule for turns 4-8
Threshold-based Wait: Holding freight at depots if the predicted congestion delay exceeds the turn-to-deliver threshold

coordination_challenges: Multiple agents may attempt to route freight simultaneously
Lower-priority freight must wait or find alternate routes

success_criteria: Agents adapt communication to topology constraints
Recovery from disruption within expected turns
Minimum aggregate idle capacity across the network during disturbance
